content: Enalapril maleate and hydrochlorothiazide are prescribed together to manage high blood pressure. Enalapril belongs to a class of medications called angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors. It works by reducing certain chemicals in the body that tighten blood vessels, allowing blood to flow more easily. Hydrochlorothiazide is a diuretic, also known as a water pill, which helps the kidneys eliminate excess water and salt through urine. This medication is available as an oral tablet and is typically taken once or twice daily, with or without food. To ensure consistent use, take it at the same time(s) each day. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take the medication exactly as directed. Do not take more or less than prescribed, and do not take it more frequently than instructed. While this medication helps control high blood pressure, it does not cure it. Continue taking it even if you feel well, and do not stop without consulting your doctor. This medication may also be prescribed for other uses. If you have questions about its other applications, ask your doctor or pharmacist for more information. Before taking enalapril and hydrochlorothiazide, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to enalapril, hydrochlorothiazide, or any other ACE inhibitors, sulfa drugs, or medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, nutritional supplements, and herbal products you are taking. Be sure to mention medications such as aspirin, NSAIDs (e.g., indomethacin), cholestyramine, colestipol, diuretics, insulin or oral diabetes medications, lithium, oral steroids (e.g., dexamethasone, methylprednisolone, prednisone), other blood pressure medications, pain medications, phenobarbital, and potassium supplements. Your doctor may need to adjust your medication doses or monitor you closely for side effects. Inform your doctor if you have or have ever had heart, parathyroid, liver, or kidney disease; lupus; diabetes; allergies; asthma; gout; or angioedema (a condition causing hives, difficulty breathing, and swelling of the face, lips, throat, tongue, hands, or feet). Let your doctor know if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. If you are undergoing surgery, including dental surgery, inform your doctor or dentist that you are taking this medication. Ask your doctor about the safe use of alcohol while on this medication, as alcohol can worsen its side effects. Be aware that diarrhea, vomiting, dehydration, and excessive sweating can lead to a drop in blood pressure, causing lightheadedness or fainting. Consult your doctor before using potassium-containing salt substitutes. If your doctor prescribes a low-salt or low-sodium diet, follow these instructions carefully. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one. This medication may cause side effects. Common side effects include cough, dizziness, headache, fatigue, muscle cramps, and decreased sexual ability. If these symptoms are severe or persistent, inform your doctor. Serious side effects, though uncommon, require immediate medical attention. These include lightheadedness, swelling of the face, throat, tongue, lips, eyes, hands, feet, ankles, or lower legs; hoarseness; difficulty breathing or swallowing; signs of infection (e.g., fever, sore throat, chills); yellowing of the skin or eyes; dry mouth; thirst; weakness; infrequent urination; upset stomach; vomiting; fainting; chest pain; or a fast or irregular heartbeat. If you experience any unusual problems while taking this medication, contact your doctor. Serious side effects can be reported to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store this medication in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excess heat and moisture (not in the bathroom). Dispose of outdated or unneeded medication properly. Consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or is not breathing, call 911 immediately. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory. Regular blood pressure checks are necessary to monitor your response to this medication. Your doctor may order lab tests to assess your body's response. Do not share this medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, ask your pharmacist. Maintain a written list of all medications, vitamins, and supplements you are taking, and bring it to all medical appointments or hospital visits. This information is also crucial in emergencies.
